title: Five and a half years with Peterson and playing 3/4 loose
summary: The trio with Sam and Louis Hayes won attention, and their loose way of playing 3/4 time amazed Peterson and freed him.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: ...and I wind up staying there 5½ years, you know, and the man never, did never win a poll as a group in his whole career, trio, and we hit the scene, you know, London House, and we started hitting all the places where the group performed,man, and everybody said man, that's the greatest trio, never sounded no better, we never, of course our style of playing, me and Louis Hayes see, Ed Thigpen, and Ray Brown.
Their style of playing, when they played a song in 3/4, they played it in 3/4.
You know, but me and Louis Hayes' style of playing in 3/4 time was different. It was loose, and they was, and he never played it 3,4,5 and it felt good to him.
And he had never played 3/4 time like that, you know.

So man, and like he was amazed, you know, he said 'Damn man, that's a different kind of feeling'. They say 1,2,3, 1,2,3, 1,2,3, boom, boom, boom, boom boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, and so me and Hayes were playing clap, clap, clap, clap, clap, clap, clap, clap, clap, clap. Like that you know.
And Oscar was amazed, you know. He said Damn, you know, I never played before like that; so that gave him freedom just to run all up and down the keyboard.
